chapter_scope: v03-c03 and v03-c04 only; remaining eight Volume 3 chapters and its assessment/project package are unfinished
review_type: Author analytic, numerical, source and instructional review; not independent certification

reviewed.reasoning: Reviewed measurable-variable/event definitions, law versus joint coupling, discrete and topological support, CDF monotonicity/right continuity/limits/jump proofs, absolutely continuous versus mixed/singular laws, binomial normalization and assumptions, Poisson normalization/recurrence/pointwise rare-event limit, exponential normalization/memorylessness/hazard, Gaussian normalization by bounded-square factorization and disk/annulus squeeze, standardization, generalized quantiles and one-to-one density changes. Reviewed expectation integrability and positive/negative parts, Cauchy principal-value failure, linearity/indicators, finite-second-moment implication, variance/affine/zero-variance/squared-loss proofs, common-law moments, joint cross-moments, covariance existence and bilinearity, correlation bound/equality, PSD covariance geometry, finite-population correction and finite-partition total expectation/variance.
reviewed.arithmetic: Independent exhaustive labeled pair sampling and Bernoulli outcome enumeration; CDF boundary checks; Poisson series with a positive omitted-tail bound; independent Simpson quadrature for exponential and Gaussian probabilities/moments with explicit tail bounds; mixed-law atoms; transformed heavy-tail and Cauchy finite-cutoff integrals. Exact rational centered and raw moments for all payoff tables, affine exposures, squared losses, joint/cross-moments, portfolio minimum certificates, all 4,845 four-file subsets, ordered pair indicator covariance and regime variance decomposition.
reviewed.solutions: All sixteen exercise prompts solved and numerical results independently recomputed. Conditions, endpoint conventions, units and interpretation accompany determinate solutions. The heavy-tail conclusions are proved by improper-integral growth, not inferred from finite numerical quadrature.
reviewed.instruction: Probability functions and integrals are defined before use. Elementary measurability refers forward to the full formal construction in Chapter 12; general transformed-expectation and independent-factorization integration results are identified as later formal foundations. Joint finite tables are introduced before covariance; full joint/conditional continuous treatment follows in Chapter 5. Population moments are distinguished from empirical estimates and from optimal decisions.
reviewed.sources: Eight method-specific official MIT PDFs retrieved and relevant method sections inspected, in addition to existing counting/probability sources. Source catalogue documents use and inspection scope. Library prose, tables, exercises and proofs are original presentations; source routes do not certify them.
reviewed.structure: Each chapter contains two worked examples, eight exercises and complete solutions, explicit boundaries/assumptions, teach-back, delayed checks and method-specific sources. Integrated generated-page/link/source/anchor checks run before acceptance.

corrections: Exhaustive pair enumeration caught an incorrect complement in the draft: at least one flag is 18/28 = 9/14, not 23/28. Corrected the manuscript and verified it against both event counts and complement arithmetic.
Specified measurability as well as integrability for the general transformed-expectation rule.
Kept the Gaussian integral normalization independent of an unstated unbounded signed-integral interchange by using finite Riemann sums and annulus bounds.
limitations: No independent human reviewer or learner trial.
Full Lebesgue integration and conditional-expectation construction remain later formal foundations; the present continuous computations use elementary absolutely convergent or nonnegative integrals.
Synthetic distribution parameters and state weights are stipulated. Their empirical estimation, fit and transport have not been claimed.
Numerical checks complement written reasoning; they do not prove general identities or infinite-tail divergence.
Visual/mobile/print UI QA remains pending after the earlier browser-policy rejection.
acceptance: Accepted by the author after completed analytic/solution/source review and successful integrated numerical/structural checks. Remaining Volume 3 chapters and package are unfinished; independent human validation and visual/mobile/print UI QA remain outstanding.
